# Spiral bacteria

> *How does a corkscrew shape let a bacterium move through tissue, and why are these bacteria so hard to see and grow?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the layout of [*Gram-positive cocci*](gram-positive-cocci.qmd). The plan:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| The group in one sentence | Thin, coiled bacteria with flagella inside the envelope, hard to stain and often impossible to culture |
| Sorting key | Reservoir (humans, ticks, rats); curved gut bacteria versus spirochaetes |
| Main organisms | *Treponema pallidum* (cannot be cultured on ordinary media), *Leptospira* (rats and flood water, Singapore relevance) |
| Supporting organisms | *Borrelia*, *Campylobacter*, *Helicobacter pylori* |
| Later in the course | Syphilis, leptospirosis and Lyme disease in the organ blocks |
